articles.title: ICC convicts CAR ex-rebel leader of crimes against humanity
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court has found Mahamat Said Abdel Kani guilty of overseeing torture and other crimes. He headed a feared prison unit that held political prisoners.

image.caption: The International Criminal Court is situated in The Hague, NetherlandsImage: Remko De Waal/ANP/AFP

blocks.text: The International Criminal Court on Wednesday convicted a former Central African Republic rebel commander on four counts of crimes against humanity committed while he was in charge of a detention center in 2013.
The court found that Mahamat Said Abdel Kani, 56, oversaw beatings and maltreatment as the country was gripped by sectarian violence.
Said also faced three counts of war crimes but was acquitted of them. During his trial, he pleaded not guilty to all charges for the crimes, which were carried out between April and August 2013.
A sentence, which could be life imprisonment, is to be handed down at a later date.

blocks.caption: The presiding judge at the trial was Miatta Maria Samba (third from L)Image: Remko De Waal/REUTERS

blocks.text: What was Said charged with?
Said was a top commander of the mainly Muslim Seleka rebel group that ousted President Francois Bozize in 2013 amid a civil war.
He was put in charge of the Central Office for the Repression of Banditry (OCRB), a prison unit in the capital, Bangui.
Prosecutors allege that prisoners at the facility, who were suspected supporters of Bozize, were subjected to various forms of torture, including whippings and body mutilation.
According to the court, inmates were also denied food or water, with some drinking their own urine out of desperation.
One cell, dubbed "the hole," where prisoners were held in dire conditions, was said by the court to be directly under Said's office.
Said stood accused of overseeing this maltreatment and personally participating in the beating of at least one prisoner, the court found.

blocks.caption: Said (R) had pleaded not guilty to all chargesImage: Remko De Waal/REUTERS

blocks.text: First trial of a Seleka member
Said was extradited to the ICC by Central African authorities in 2021, with his trial beginning in September 2022.
It is the first time that a member of the Seleka group has stood trial at the ICC.
The ICC, established in The Hague in 2022, is the world's only independent tribunal capable of prosecuting those accused of the world's worst crimes.

articles.title: As the EU advances free trade with Southeast Asia, why is there no ASEAN-wide deal?
articles.summary: After years of arduous negotiations, the EU is closing on a string of bilateral trade deals with countries in Southeast Asia. And yet, a bloc-to-bloc agreement between the EU and ASEAN remains a…

image.caption: The Philippines is one of the many ASEAN countries pursuing closer ties with the EUImage: Ezra Acayan/AFP

blocks.text: The EU and several Southeast Asian nations are nearing the finish line on bilateral trade deals, and if the current deadlines hold, the European bloc will have agreements in place with six out of 11 ASEAN states by the middle of next year.

Free trade agreements with Singapore and Vietnam are already in force. Negotiations with Indonesia have concluded, and Jakarta aims to sign the agreement in October, with implementation targeted for early 2027.
Trade Reset: How Europe is replacing China and the US

Talks with Thailand, relaunched in 2023, have reached nine negotiating rounds, while Malaysia resumed negotiations in early 2025 after a 13-year pause. Both are expected to be finalized by the end of the year or early 2027.
Earlier this week, the EU and the Philippines announced that they had reached "substantial agreement" on their free trade agreement, putting it on course for formal conclusion in the coming months.
Trade up by more than half in single decade
Speaking to DW, Chris Humphrey, executive director of the EU-ASEAN Business Council, described EU engagement with ASEAN on trade and investment issues as "at an all-time high."
EU-Southeast Asia goods trade reached €274.9 billion ($313.7 billion) last year, up around 6% from the previous year and more than 50% from the €177.9 billion recorded in 2016, according to EU data.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is now the EU's third-largest goods trading partner outside Europe, behind only the United States and China.
The Philippines is chair of ASEAN — these are its goals

This week, Manila hosted both the ASEAN–EU Business Summit and the 22nd meeting of ASEAN economic ministers and the EU's trade commissioner. The two blocs pledged greater cooperation to protect themselves from rising geopolitical tensions, including unilateral trade actions and regional conflicts, that "collectively threaten the rules-based international order."
Why is Southeast Asia so important for Europe?

Brussels is expanding its network of trade agreements globally as it looks to expand to new markets and form more resilient supply chains. Southeast Asia, in turn, sits at the center of supply chains for semiconductors, electronics, electric vehicles and batteries, with investment pouring into data centers, renewable energy and digital services.
EU-Mercosur free trade deal: Who gains the most?
An article published this month by the International Monetary Fund said ASEAN's 11 economies already form a $4.5 trillion bloc, growing at more than 4.5% a year.
Such economic expansion, combined with multinational firms' efforts to diversify production beyond China, has made access to Southeast Asian markets more attractive for European companies.

Alfred Gerstl, an expert on Indo-Pacific international relations at the University of Vienna, told DW that geopolitical and geo-economic changes are also accelerating cooperation between the two regions.

US President Donald Trump's "protectionist and erratic trade policies" have acted as a crucial catalyst, he said, while the EU's strategy of "de-risking from China" and diversifying supply chains boosted Southeast Asia's strategic importance.

A stronger partnership with European nations also plays in favor of Southeast Asia governments, who have long tried to maintain broad economic relationships with competing powers rather than becoming excessively dependent on China, the United States or any other single partner.
EU companies push for an ASEAN-wide deal

The EU-ASEAN Business Council, said Humphrey, is calling for a region-to-region economic framework with a clear pathway to an eventual region-to-region free trade deal, "something European business has consistently called for."
"This would adopt a modular approach, perhaps starting with a region-to-region Digital Trade Agreement and an Investment Protection Agreement," Humphrey told DW.

The idea is not exactly new — the EU and ASEAN launched negotiations for a region-to-region agreement in 2007, but the talks bogged down over enormous differences between ASEAN economies and disagreements over the agreement's scope.
The talks were put on ice by mutual agreement in 2009, after which Brussels switched to negotiating bilateral deals with individual ASEAN members.

The main difficulty preservers to this day, as ASEAN includes Singapore, one of the world's wealthiest economies, alongside developing and least-developed members, making it difficult to agree on common commitments acceptable to Brussels.
"In addition, meeting the EU's high social, labor and environmental standards is difficult for the less-developed ASEAN members," said Gerstl.
Is the Commission ready to up the stakes?

Yet, even without an immediate prospect of a full region-to-region agreement, completing the current bilateral deals would give the EU preferential trade arrangements with most of ASEAN's largest economies and demonstrate that Southeast Asia has moved higher up Brussels' trade agenda.
For Humphrey, however, that should be the starting point rather than the endpoint. The concern, he said, is the European Commission might not be willing to move towards region-to-region agreements.

"With 2027 marking the 50th Anniversary of EU-ASEAN relations, we remain hopeful that the Commission will take this milestone seriously and ramp up work on a region-to-region economic architecture," he told DW.
"Failing to do so will only make ASEAN think that the EU does not take the region seriously."

articles.title: Tigray forces seize main airport in northern Ethiopia from police, residents tell the BBC
articles.summary: There are fears of a return to war in the northern region as tensions between the government and TPLF escalate.

blocks.text: Local forces in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray have seized control of the airport in the regional capital, Mekelle, from federal police, local residents have told the BBC.

No flights are currently landing at the airport and Ethiopian Airlines said it had suspended flights to Mekelle and the cities of Shire and Axum because of what it called the "current situation" in Tigray.
There have been escalating tensions this year between the government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that runs Tigray, fuelling fears of a return to civil war.
On Sunday, the TPLF announced an alliance with six armed groups in Ethiopia to remove the government in Addis Ababa.
A two-year war in Tigray ended in November 2022 - but both sides are now accusing each other of violating an African Union-mediated peace deal.
It was one of the most-deadly conflicts this century, with the AU's mediator estimating some 600,000 people died as the fighting drove the region to the precipice of famine.
The flight suspension follows a series of reported drone strikes in Tigray.
On Tuesday, a strike in the southern town of Alamata killed at least 14 people and injured 22 others, according to the Tigrayan authorities.
The town's mayor, Mogos Shiferaw, told the BBC that more than five drones and one fighter jet had carried out more than 21 strikes beginning at around 03:30.
"This caused a lot of psychological trauma in our city and our people were in a state of panic," he said.
Mogos said all those killed and injured were civilians, accusing federal forces of targeting two secondary schools.
He believed they were struck on suspicion that they were being used by Tigrayan forces.
But the mayor said the schools, which had served as federal military bases during the civil war, were unoccupied as the academic year had not yet begun.
The BBC has not independently verified the allegations and the government has not publicly commented.
On Wednesday, the Tigray authorities accused Addis Ababa of launching an open invasion on the region's residents, urging people to support the regional forces and maintain unity.
Meanwhile, the US State Department's Bureau of African Affairs has condemned a separate drone strike that it said took place on Monday, targeting a convoy of Catholic vehicles carrying food aid.
It called for an investigation and urged all parties to resolve their differences through dialogue and take steps to prevent similar incidents.
Both Addis Ababa and TPLF leaders have faced criticism over delays in implementing key provisions of the Pretoria Agreement, which formally ended the conflict in November 2022.
In July, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed accused the TPLF of preparing for renewed conflict during an address to parliament.
Just before the general election in May, the TPLF restored its pre-war administration, disbanding an interim one appointed by Abiy.
There have also been reports that the TPLF has forcibly recruiting young men to join its forces.

items: Carlos Yulo led the Philippine gymnastics team to a sixth-place finish in the men's artistic gymnastics team all-around event at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.

Carlos Yulo showed strong individual performances, posting the highest score in floor exercise and competing for medals in upcoming finals for floor exercise, vault, and parallel bars.

MANILA, Philippines – Carlos Yulo anchored the Philippines to a sixth-place finish in the team all-around event of the men’s artistic gymnastics in the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, as he and his teammates got some practice in before the apparatus finals in the coming days.
The team, composed of Carlos, his younger brother Eldrew, Juancho Miguel Besana, Justine Ace de Leon, and Zachary Nunez, totaled 227.359 points across the six apparatuses in the eight-team final.
China topped the event for the third consecutive edition, registering 255.095 points to edge reigning Olympic champion Japan for the gold.
Despite being led by Olympic individual all-around gold medalists Daiki Hashimoto and Shinnosuke Oka, Japan settled for silver with 253.826 points.
Chinese Taipei finished a distant third with 239.896 points for the bronze, while Kazakhstan (237.596) and South Korea (236.359) placed fourth and fifth, respectively, ahead of the Philippines.
Set to compete in the floor exercise, vault, and parallel bars finals, Carlos showed medal-winning potential, with a gold also well within reach.
Carlos posted the highest mark in floor exercise with 14.266 points, netted the fourth-best score in vault with 14.566, and tied for the fifth-highest mark in parallel bars with 14.166.

Meanwhile, Eldrew recorded 13.966 points in vault, 13.166 in horizontal bar, 13.0 in floor exercise, 12.233 in rings, 11.933 in parallel bars, and 11.366 in pommel horse — the only one in the team to see action in all apparatuses.
In the team event, only three of the five gymnasts compete in each apparatus, with their scores combined to determine the total.

De Leon contributed 13.833 points in vault, 12.533 in rings, and 10.933 in floor exercise, Nunez added 12.333 in pommel horse and 12.066 in horizontal bar, while Besana chipped in 11.933 points in pommel horse, 11.733 in horizontal bar, and 10.0 in parallel bars as the Philippines came in ahead of Vietnam (214.428) and Singapore (200.928).
Aside from Carlos, Eldrew vies for a medal in floor exercise and horizontal bar, while Besana shoots for a podium finish in vault.

articles.title: Trump to meet China’s Xi as Congress mulls bill banning artificial superintelligence – US politics live
articles.summary: Congress has so far done little to rein in the AI industry even as some of its most prominent leaders warn about potentially catastrophic risks

blocks.text: Key events

items: 9m agoTrump to meet with China's Xi as Congress mulls bill banning artificial superintelligence

blocks.text: Trump to meet with China's Xi as Congress mulls bill banning artificial superintelligence
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Donald Trump will meet with the Chinese president Xi Jinping later today, ahead of a three-day visit that will undoubtedly see artificial intelligence (AI) high on the agenda.
António Guterres, the UN secretary general, has called on the two countries to establish a dialogue on AI similar to the communication between the US and the Soviet Union during the cold war.
“Governments with the greatest AI capabilities have the greatest responsibilities to humanity, to establish channels for dialogue, transparency, trust and cooperation,” Guterres said.

Tech executives including Jeff Bezos of Amazon, Sundar Pichai of Alphabet, Sam Altman of ⁠OpenAI, Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk ​of ​Tesla, Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Jensen Huang ​of Nvidia will reportedly ​attend a ⁠state dinner at the White House on Thursday evening.

It comes as two leading progressive US lawmakers, senator Bernie Sanders and representative Greg Casar, were due to unveil legislation later today that would ban artificial superintelligence and create a federal agency to oversee advanced AI.

The bill, provided first to the Associated Press, would also pause advanced AI development until guidelines are implemented while creating the Department of Artificial Intelligence. Multiple employees at leading AI companies are endorsing the bill.

“It doesn’t take a genius to say, ‘slow it down,’” Sanders said in an interview with AP. “Do we really want to develop a super intelligence that when it becomes smarter than human beings could act independently of human control? I don’t think we do.”
Congress has so far done little to rein in the AI industry even as some of its most prominent leaders warn about potentially catastrophic risks.
Xi departed Beijing on Wednesday, state media said, heading to Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, where he will be met by Trump on the tarmac.

“President Xi Jinping left Beijing by special plane for a state visit to the United States” accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.
In other developments:

items: Speaking at the UN general assembly, Donald Trump re-issued his threat to “annihilate” Iran and “drive them into Hell” if the regime didn’t capitulate and make a deal.” He also said he was “working closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine” to end the disastrous war, defended his administration’s actions in Latin America – including the midnight raid to arrest former Venezuelan president Nicólas Maduro, defended his drone strikes on boats in the Caribbean and the Pacific, accused Mexico of being effectively controlled by the cartels, and said it was “unacceptable” for the US to share a border with a nation under such conditions, pointed to regime change in Cuba and said he would reject any calls for a “globalist scheme” to control artificial intelligence.

Shortly after his UN address, Trump signed a Greenland deal, which Greenland’s prime minister Jens-Frederick Nielsen said “underlines the importance of the Nato alliance.” In tricky, carefully worded paragraphs, she said the agreement “recognises the US defining historical and ongoing contributions to the security and defence of Greenland,” but it also “respects the sovereignty and the territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as Greenland’s right to self-determination.”

Trump told a CNN reporter at the UN general assembly on Tuesday that he was “surprised” the outlet was covering him, saying it ‘shouldn’t be here’ after he banned the network alongside Politico and MS Now from the White House on Friday.

At a joint press conference on Tuesday, vice-president JD Vance and Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, announced that the federal government was removing 760,000 enrollees from Affordable Care Act insurance marketplaces.

articles.title: Angry Anderson, rock star who soundtracked Kylie's wedding in Neighbours, dies aged 79
articles.summary: He fronted the rock band Rose Tattoo, but became best known for his solo hit Suddenly.

blocks.text: Rock star Angry Anderson, whose music famously soundtracked the wedding of Kylie Minogue and Jason Donovan's characters in Australian TV soap Neighbours, has died at the age of 79.
The musician, whose real name was Gary Anderson, rose to fame with rock band Rose Tattoo, which he fronted from 1976.

His solo song Suddenly became a global hit after it was played during the wedding of Minogue and Donovan's characters Scott and Charlene in Neighbours. The wedding episode was watched by 20 million people in the UK alone in 1988.
Anderson said Minogue had been "adamant" that the track was used for the scene, and he later declared that Suddenly was the best song he had ever written.
Before his death, Anderson had a cardiac arrest while on Rose Tattoo's farewell tour in Europe last month.
He was treated in hospital before going home to Australia, and the band cancelled nine live dates.
A joint statement, external from Anderson's family and Rose Tattoo remembered him as a "devoted father, and much-loved bandmate".
"His loss will be deeply felt by all those who knew and loved him both here in Australia and overseas," it said.
"We thank everyone for their prayers and messages of love and continued support."
Born in Melbourne in 1947, Anderson and Rose Tattoo first became known on Australia's rock scene, releasing five albums beginning with their 1978 debut.
After the band split nine years later, Anderson continued recording music as a solo artist, and co-wrote and released Suddenly in the summer of 1987.
It was quickly selected by Minogue for use in Neighbours for her character Charlene Mitchell's wedding to Donovan's Scott Robinson.
Thanks in large part to its use in Neighbours, Suddenly reached the top three in both the UK and Australia.
However, it was held off the number one spot in its home country by Minogue's own debut solo single, Locomotion.
Anderson released two albums as a solo artist, before Rose Tattoo reunited in 1993 to support Guns N' Roses on their Australian tour.
The band returned in 1998 for their own tour and were inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) Hall of Fame in 2006.
Anderson's other credits included playing Herod in an Australian production of Jesus Christ Superstar.
He was made a Member of the Order of Australia in 1993, in recognition of service to the community, particularly his charity work and his work as a youth advocate.

articles.title: South Sudan's president dissolves government ahead of country's first elections
articles.summary: South Sudan has not held elections since independence in 2011 - polls have twice been postponed.
articles.byline: Nichola Mandil, Akisa Wandera, Allan Olingo

blocks.text: South Sudan President Salva Kiir has dissolved the transitional government, three months before the country's first election since its independence in 2011.
The country has previously postponed elections twice and extended the transitional period several times.
Under the amended law, signed on Monday, Kiir removed the country's five vice-presidents and dissolved parliament, as well as national and state governments.

Kiir is the presidential candidate of his Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM). No prominent figures have announced plans to challenge him in the December poll. The main opposition leader Riek Machar was sacked as vice-president last year and charged with treason.
He is under house arrest.
Machar had been named vice-president as part of a 2018 peace deal to end a five-year civil war between forces loyal to the two men.

Kiir will remain in office with full constitutional powers until an elected president is sworn in. He also reappointed some ministers and governors in caretaker positions until the 22 December elections.

Ahead of Tuesday's announcement a heavy security presence was reported in the capital, Juba. Soldiers from the army and national security services blocked access to government ministries. Soldiers were also seen patrolling parts of the city.
A senior government official told the BBC that staff arriving for work were turned away and told to return the following Monday.
UN agencies in Juba also asked staff to work remotely while the situation was monitored.
Kiir last week dismissed the chairman of the national elections commission, Abednego Akok Kacuol, without giving a reason. He was replaced by the commission's secretary-general, Gabriel Bol Deng.
Akok had said in August that the commission needed $250m (£190m) to conduct the election but had received only $21m.
In June, the main opposition group, the Sudan People's Liberation Movement in Opposition (SPLM-IO), the party of Machar, warned people not to take part in poll preparations.

"Anyone coming to register voters and campaign in territories controlled by the mighty SPLM-IO, you will be a prisoner of war," Nathaniel Pierino, acting chairperson of the group, said in a post on Facebook.
The body which oversees implementation of the 2018 peace agreement, the Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC), said South Sudan had entered a "critical phase".

It said several key talks under the agreement remained incomplete and urged the parties to agree on a path towards credible elections and a peaceful end to the transitional period, which has lasted since independence.
The latest 24-month extension was due to end on 22 February 2027.

articles.title: Munich, Berlin, Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's three Olympic candidates
articles.summary: Munich, Berlin, or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Three candidates are in the running, with one city considered the slight favorite.

image.caption: Munich's Olympic Stadium was the main venue for the 1972 Summer OlympicsImage: Jonas Lohrmann/DZBA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany is hoping to win the right to host the Olympic Games in 2036, 2040 or 2044. On Saturday, the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) is to meet to vote on which of three bids (Munich, Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr, Berlin) to throw its support behind.
Munich: Political and public support

The motto of Munich's Olympic bid is "For Games with heart and soul." The concept focuses on sustainability, with the 1972 Olympic Park serving as the centerpiece. According to documents published by the bid committee, around 90% of the competition venues are located less than 30 kilometers (18.6 miles) from the Olympic Village. Most of the venues that would be used already exist, with only a few temporary facilities to be constructed.

In addition to existing infrastructure, other advantages include Munich's experience in hosting major sporting events and its Olympic legacy from 1972. The organizers aim to offer an alternative model to the pricey Olympic projects of the past.

blocks.caption: Munich's bid would lean heavily on already existing venuesImage: Frank Hoermann/SvenSimon/picture alliance

blocks.text: Political support for the Munich bid is strong: "In Munich, we have the perfect conditions to host the Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games," Munich Mayor Dominik Krause is quoted as saying on the city website, "muenchen.de."

"Hosting the Olympic Games in Munich would be an investment in the future — not only because of the immense social value but also due to the resulting acceleration of key urban development and infrastructure projects. Munich is ready for the Olympics!"
Munich residents also appear to support the bid. In a city referendum held last October, just over 305,000 residents cast their votes, with 66.4% voting in favor of an Olympic bid.
Berlin: Political opposition and a the weight of history

The situation is different in Germany's capital. The Left Party (Die Linke) won the most votes in Sunday's election in Berlin, meaning Elif Eralp, its chairperson, could become the city-state's new governing mayor. She is on the record as opposing the idea of bringing the Games to the capital, describing the bid as a "waste of taxpayer money." The Green Party, a potential coalition partner for Eralp, also opposes an Olympic bid.

blocks.caption: Berlin's Olympic Stadium is at the heart of the capital's bid to host a future Summer Games Image: Andreas Gora/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The prospect of hosting the Games in 2036 has sparked further debate. Critics point to the 1936 Berlin Olympics, which were exploited by Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime as a propaganda tool. Proponents, however, argue that the 2036 Games could showcase the values ​​of a democratic and cosmopolitan Germany.
Berlin's bid also envisages mainly using existing sports facilities for the Games.

"Ninety-seven percent of the required sports facilities already exist. Apart from one privately financed arena, we do not need to build any new venues," said Kaweh Niroomand, Berlin's Olympic commissioner, told the "Die Welt" newspaper.
"The Games should fit Berlin — not Berlin the Games."
Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr: Sustainability and public support

Unlike Munich and Berlin, this third bid encompasses an entire region, featuring numerous venues that are widely dispersed. Cologne would serve as the "lead city" in the bid that features 15 municipalities in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia. Cologne would host the Olympic Village and a temporary athletics stadium.

Organizers highlight the fact that all of the venues either already exist or would be temporary and to the fact that 66% of those who voted in lasts April's referenda in the affected municipalities voted in favor of the bid.

blocks.caption: Schalke's football stadium would be temporarily transformed into swimming venue with a capacity of 60,000Image: Marcus Hirnschal/osnapix/picture alliance

blocks.text: Apart from sustainability, the Rhine-Ruhr region's dense sports infrastructure is considered a key strength. A potential drawback is the location of competitions across many cities in Germany's most densely populated region. Traffic jams are a daily occurrence and many trains run late or are cancelled altogether.
Munich with a slight edge

A total of 144 votes are up for grabs in Saturday's vote. Eligible to vote are Germany's 42 Olympic sports federations — including those for winter sports — along with the 10-member DOSB Executive Board and eight individual DOSB members. The individual sports federations each hold three votes.

If none of the three bids wins an absolute majority in the first round of voting, the last-placed bid drops out for the second round – meaning a decision will come after no more than two rounds of voting.
The final report by a DOSB evaluation commission makes Munich's bid the slight favorite, with 87.03 out of a possible 100 points, ahead of Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr (85.02) and Berlin (74.64).

This is just the next step in a long process of deciding who will host the next three Olympic Summer Games. The International Olympic Committee isn't to decide on who will host the 2036 Olympics until 2029.
This article was adapted from German.

articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years
articles.summary:
Sunil Bharti Mittal’s Airtel Money targets $9bn IPO in boost for ailing UK stock market

A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire…

blocks.text: A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange.
Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures.

The company is understood to be hoping to raise about $800m (£601m) from the initial public offering (IPO) and is targeting a valuation of $8bn to $9bn, which would make it one of London’s largest listings in recent years.
Airtel Money has 53 million monthly active users across 13 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, including Uganda, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

blocks.caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal controls Bharti Enterprises. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: It operates through a network of branches and kiosks, which enable customers to load money on to their phones, withdraw cash and access other money services, and the company generated revenues of just under $1.4bn in the last financial year.

Airtel Money’s parent company is Airtel Africa, a telecoms provider that is part of the Indian conglomerate Bharti Enterprises, which is ultimately controlled by the billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal. Airtel Africa is already listed on the FTSE 100 but said it wanted Airtel Money to be listed separately.
“From a company perspective, [the listing] gives us flexibility for the future,” said Airtel Money’s chief executive, Ian Ferrao.

“We evaluated multiple [stock] exchanges, including the Middle East because we’ve got a headquarters in Dubai, along with European and North American exchanges. Ultimately, shareholders felt that London was the right choice. We still believe there is deep capital available … all the global institutional investors are here.”
Ferrao added: “Most importantly there’s a deep understanding of emerging markets in the London market and Africa specifically.”

Airtel Money said it would announce more details about the float in early October, including the indicative price range and number of shares to be offered, with final pricing to follow later in the month.

Airtel Africa had originally targeted a listing in the first six months of 2026 but delayed it to the second half of the year, blaming unfavourable market conditions as a result of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Several other companies also pushed back planned IPOs amid the market volatility caused by the conflict.
after newsletter promotion

Airtel Africa owns just under 78% of Airtel Money and will remain a long-term investor after the IPO. Minority stakes are held by TPG, ​Mastercard, the Qatar Investment Authority and Chimetech Holding.
Revenue in Airtel Money’s most recent quarter to 30 June climbed 38% to £399m, according to Airtel Africa.

The decision to float Airtel Money in the UK could mark a turning point for the City, which has struggled to attract listings in recent times and has also been hit by departures, partly as a result of overseas takeovers of UK companies.

Airtel Money’s planned listing could be one of the biggest debuts since the international payments company Wise floated in 2021 with a valuation of £8.75bn. Wise has since moved its main listing from London to New York.

articles.title: Hurricane Polo in the Pacific Ocean considered 'one of the strongest storms ever'
articles.summary: Hurricane Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades, and it was expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast as a Category 5 storm.

image.caption: This photo provided by National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration shows Hurricane Polo strengthening in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Mexico on Tuesday. (NOAA/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
Hurricane Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades, and it was expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast as a Category 5 storm.
Polo not expected to make landfall, but its gathering strength is 'truly remarkable,' storm researcher says
Hurricane Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades and was expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast as a Category 5 storm.
Polo was an "extremely dangerous" storm, with maximum sustained winds of 265 km/h, the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami said Tuesday night.

Polo was nearly stationary early Wednesday, about 300 kilometres south of Zihuatanejo in Guerrero state and 540 kilometres southeast of Manzanillo, moving north at four kilometres per hour with maximum sustained winds of 255 km/h, the centre reported.
It was forecast to turn sharply to the northwest during the day and then move in west-northwest over the next several days.

U.S. National Hurricane Center data shows Polo's winds reached speeds comparable to only a few hurricanes in the region in recent decades, primarily Hurricane Patricia, which had winds that reached 346 km/h in 2015.
"This is one of the strongest storms ever in the [Pacific] Basin," said Kristen L. Corbosiero, professor at the University at Albany's department of atmospheric and environmental sciences.
I’ve tracked El Niño for years — I’ve never seen this before

The rapid intensification of the storm has stunned scientists and authorities alike, with the NHC writing in a report that it was "truly remarkable" how quickly Polo gained strength in the past 24 hours.

Phil Klotzbach, research scientist in the department of atmospheric science at Colorado State University, attributed the intensification to the weather phenomenon known as El Niño, which has fuelled crippling droughts in Mexico and Central America and floods in other parts of the region.
In the Pacific, it has resulted in warmer waters and wind patterns that act as fodder for hurricanes, he said.
"There are all the ingredients that hurricanes need to get really strong really fast," Klotzbach said.
Warnings of life-threatening flooding

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said experts indicated that the hurricane was not likely to touch land. Still, hurricane-force winds extend up to 65 kilometres from the storm's centre and tropical storm-force winds up to 169 kilometres from the eye, the U.S. centre said.

Heavy rain could produce flash flooding and mudslides. About eight to 15 centimetres of rain was forecast for Guerrero and Michoacán states, with smaller amounts possible for coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima and Jalisco states.
The U.S. Embassy in Mexico issued a weather alert, instructing citizens to avoid water and beaches and to heed warnings from Mexican authorities.

"Even if the storm does not make direct landfall, heavy rain may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides. Hazardous ocean conditions — intensified by storms — may result in deadly rip currents and rogue waves," the embassy wrote in a statement.
Tropical storm conditions were expected along the Pacific coast in Guerrero, Michoacan and Colima states Wednesday into Thursday.

The hurricane set residents along Mexico's Pacific coast on edge once again after being walloped by a number of powerful cyclones in recent years. Beaches emptied and dark clouds swirled above choppy seas, while Mexican authorities temporarily suspended classes Tuesday in a number of areas.

items: It's almost the end of September. Where are the Atlantic hurricanes?
Is this Super El Nino a peek into forever weather?

blocks.text: Mexico's navy shut down ports in the states of Guerrero and Michoacán and warned civilians and fishermen to take care.

Concepción López Villegas was busily preparing her seaside restaurant for what may come. Strong waves were already lapping at the coastline of her city, Lázaro Cárdenas in Michoacán. As men and children watched the stirring waters behind her, López Villegas said she feared powerful waves would destroy the small business she has worked decades to build.
"We're worried and trying to protect our businesses," López Villegas said. "And of course, we're sad because it's our heritage, our legacy that from one moment to another could be destroyed."

Meanwhile, Odalys strengthened to a Category 1 hurricane early Wednesday and was about 2,085 kilometres off the southern tip of Baja California in Mexico, with maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h, the hurricane centre said.
LISTEN | Experts discuss what could transpire in months ahead:
What on Earth?25:02Is this Super El Niño a peek into forever weather?
Pacific-Atlantic contrast

Polo is the third Category 5 hurricane of the Pacific season, following Genevieve and Lowell earlier this year. Category 5 is the highest level on the Saffir-Simpson scale, reflecting that a storm has maximum sustained winds exceeding 253 kilometres per hour.

In the U.S., California Gov. Gavin Newsom on Monday declared a state of emergency in order to marshal state resources over the potential impacts of El Niño ahead of the winter season. The order directs stage agencies to prepare roads and critical infrastructure for the risk of floods and landslides in vulnerable communities.

The developments in the Pacific come as a new research report released Wednesday by the University of Chicago-based Climate Impact Lab says El Niño, combined with the record global heat it is driving, could lead to tens of thousands of more heat-related deaths over the next six months.
The heaviest toll, the lab said, is expected in poorer countries, particularly in the Southern Hemisphere.
In contrast to the Pacific, no hurricanes have formed yet this year in the Atlantic Ocean. The effects of El Niño have so far crushed storms before they develop.

articles.title: Paolo Duterte: Let Supreme Court decide if impeachment threshold rule legal
articles.summary: Davao City Representative Paolo Duterte questioned Wednesday the legality of the Senate impeachment court's decision to base the two-thirds vote to convict his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, on…

blocks.text: Published September 23, 2026 6:56pm

Davao City Representative Paolo Duterte questioned Wednesday the legality of the Senate impeachment court's decision to base the two-thirds vote to convict his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, on the number of senators who are capable of participating in the trial proceedings.

With 13 yes votes, one no vote, and six non-participants, the Senate impeachment court effectively set aside an earlier ruling that placed the votes needed to convict the vice president at 16. The voting threshold is still two-thirds, but absentee senators will no longer be counted.

"Is it within its authority as the impeachment court? But the bigger question remains—does that interpretation conform to the Constitution? The Constitution says conviction requires the concurrence of two-thirds of ALL the Members of the Senate," Paolo Duterte said.
The vice president's lead defense counsel, Sheila Sison, manifested before the impeachment court that her client will exhaust all legal remedies following the senator-judges' ruling.
Under the 1987 Constitution, the Senate has the sole power to try and decide on all impeachment cases.

Sharing their expert views as amici curiae as invited by the Senate impeachment court, three former Supreme Court chief justices said the meaning of two-thirds under Senate rules is not rigid to mean 16, and can be changed by senator-judges.
However, the Davao City congressman said that with the Senate voting what is meant by "all members" meant, it also raised a constitutional question.

"If the affected party chooses to bring that question before the Supreme Court, then let the High Court decide whether the Senate's interpretation is consistent with the fundamental law," Duterte said.
"At the end of the day, positions in government are temporary. The Constitution is not," Duterte said.
Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo clarified that the threshold was not changed per se. If an absentee senator opted to show up on the day of voting, they will be counted in the computation of the two-thirds.

Senators Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada are currently detained at the Quezon City Jail for separate plunder charges. Senator Loren Legarda is on extended medical leave, while Senator Ronaldo "Bato" dela Rosa has been missing following the issuance of an arrest warrant against him by the the International Criminal Court. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Sen. Gatchalian calls for stricter gun rules after South Cotabato shooting
articles.summary: Senate President Win Gatchalian on Wednesday stricter gun regulations in the aftermath of the South Cotabato school shooting that left three students dead.

blocks.text: Published September 23, 2026 6:54pm
Senate President Win Gatchalian on Wednesday stricter gun regulations in the aftermath of the South Cotabato school shooting that left three students dead.

“I call for a review of the rules and protocols governing the issuance of firearms to government personnel. Re-examine standards for safekeeping, storage, and ensuring that access to weapons never reaches untrained hands, especially children,” Gatchalian said in a privilege speech during Wednesday’s plenary session. Gatchalian also pushed for early detection when it came to mental health struggles.

“Let us take care not to stigmatize anyone with mental health struggles, especially those who have the courage to ask for help, because they do not make a person violent. Our objective must be early detection, intervention, and support, so that qualified professional help reaches a distressed child, and that credible threats are assessed properly before anyone is harmed,” he added.
Gatchalian asked the public to remain calm amid these shootings, saying that while it is easy to get mad and look for someone to blame, there needs to be proper sharing of information.
Authorities have suspected that the shooter may have been influenced by online elements. He also urged Meta to block or stop the spreading of these types of videos on social media.
The Senate President said he also supported the passing of the Comprehensive School Safety Act and the Child Online Safety Protection Act.

The Comprehensive School Safety Act mandated every educational institution to have a School Safety Plan, and prohibited acts of violence, bullying, digital harm and more. It was passed on the third and final reading at the Senate, a few days after the South Cotabato school shooting.
Meanwhile, the Child Online Safety Protection Act aims to provide stronger protection for children against online sexual abuse and exploitation.

The school shooting in Banga National High School in South Cotabato is the third school shooting that resulted in multiple deaths. In June, two students opened fire on their classmates in a Tacloban school, killing three others.
In August, another student killed his schoolmate in Ateneo de Zamboanga before turning the gun on himself. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: DOF backs excise tax relief on LPG, kerosene, but not diesel or gasoline
articles.summary: Finance Secretary Frederick Go says broader relief could cost P12 billion a month in lost revenue.

blocks.text: September 23, 2026 | 6:47pm
Workers handle liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders at an outlet in Quezon City on Tuesday, March 31, 2026.
The STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Finance Secretary Frederick Go has signed a resolution seeking the suspension of excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene, while holding off on similar relief for diesel and gasoline over concerns about who would benefit and the potential P12-billion monthly revenue loss.

Go announced the move during the Department of Finance's Senate budget hearing on Tuesday, September 22, after Sen. Bong Go asked what the government was doing to cushion consumers from rising oil prices.

"Actually kanina mga 15 minutes ago, pumipirma ako dito. Pinirmahan ko iyong resolution to remove excise taxes on LPG and kerosene, which is very similar to what we did in the first round of the Middle East War," the finance chief said.

(Actually, about 15 minutes ago, I was signing it here. I signed the resolution to remove excise taxes on LPG and kerosene, which is very similar to what we did in the first round of the Middle East War.)
The resolution still requires the approval of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. before the tax suspension can take effect.

Under Republic Act 12316, the president may suspend or reduce excise taxes on specific petroleum products upon the recommendation of the Development Budget Coordination Committee and in coordination with the energy secretary once the average Dubai crude price reaches or exceeds $80 per barrel for a month.
The Department of Energy certified on September 15 that the benchmark had been breached, with Dubai crude averaging $99.41 per barrel from August 13 to September 11.
The law allows excise tax relief to last for up to three months.
Earlier Tuesday, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the government's recommendation on fuel excise tax relief was expected to reach Marcos within the week.
The move would effectively revive relief granted earlier this year, when Marcos suspended excise taxes on LPG and kerosene for three months beginning in April.
Not for diesel, gasoline
The economic team, however, is not recommending the suspension of excise taxes on diesel and gasoline for now.
"Ang conclusion po ng DBCC nung una namin itong pinag-usapan ay, number one, if you remove taxes on diesel and gasoline, it will not be progressive," Go said.
(The DBCC's conclusion when we first discussed this was, number one, that removing taxes on diesel and gasoline would not be progressive.)
Go said the DBCC's assessment was that higher-income consumers would receive a larger share of the benefit because they consume more gasoline and diesel.
"So we thought for that point is to keep the taxes and instead do a targeted subsidy to the vulnerable sectors," Go said.
The finance chief also said suspending excise taxes on gasoline and diesel would cost the government around P12 billion in revenue each month.
"In the absence of any revenue enhancing measure to replace the P12 billion a month that we will lose, in the meantime the DBCC is not endorsing that to the president," Go said.
The government has instead favored targeted assistance for sectors most affected by rising fuel costs, including fuel subsidies for public transport drivers.

articles.title: Prosecution dismisses Sal Panelo's warning on impeachment vote threshold
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel brushed aside former presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo's claim that senator-judges who voted to change the basis for determining the threshold to convict Vice…

blocks.text: Published September 23, 2026 6:42pm

The House prosecution panel brushed aside former presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo's claim that senator-judges who voted to change the basis for determining the threshold to convict Vice President Sara Duterte violated the Constitution.
Panelo, who served as chief presidential legal counsel to Duterte's father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, described the impeachment court's ruling as a tragedy.

“Ang ginawa nila ay talagang nakalulungkot at isang trahedya na nilabag nila ang Saligang Batas nang lantaran. Dahil hindi talaga sila maaaring bumoto sa isang isyu na ang utos ng Saligang Batas ay hindi na nila dapat pakialaman,” he told reporters.
(What they did is truly saddening and a tragedy — they blatantly violated the Constitution. They cannot vote on an issue where the Constitution dictates that they should no longer meddle.)

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday voted to interpret the constitutional requirement of a two-thirds vote based on the number of senators who are “legally and factually capable of participating” in the impeachment proceedings.
The ruling effectively overturned presiding officer Senator-judge Francis “Chiz” Escudero's July 6 ruling that 16 votes, or two-thirds of all 24 senators, would be needed to convict Duterte.

Thirteen senator-judges voted in favor of a motion by Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo to reconsider Escudero's July 6 ruling, following the continued absence or inability of some senators to participate in the impeachment trial.

The vote came after the Senate impeachment court heard the views of four former justices of the Supreme Court who served as amici curiae, lengthy oral arguments from both the prosecution and defense, and probing questions from senator-judges on the constitutional basis for determining the two-thirds voting threshold.
Panelo also said that senator-judges who vote under the new formula could face criminal liability.

“Pag sila ay bumoto under a new threshold, which is violative of the Constitution, they open themselves to Article 204 of the Revised Penal Code under that provision. Ang sabi po doon, if you knowingly render an unjust judgment, you are criminally liable,” he said.

(If they vote under a new threshold, which is violative of the Constitution, they open themselves up to Article 204 of the Revised Penal Code. It says that if you knowingly render an unjust judgment, you are criminally liable.)

Panelo had previously argued that the impeachment court could not alter the constitutional requirement that two-thirds of all Senate members must concur in a conviction. He also warned that senator-judges could face legal challenges and possible criminal cases if they proceeded with changing the voting requirement.
However, private prosecutors Lorna Kapunan and Amando Ligutan appeared unfazed by Panelo's comments.
“Who is he? Don't know him,” Kapunan told reporters.
“Not familiar, sorry,” Ligutan said.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Iran denies dropping preconditions amid ‘very productive’ three-hour UN talks in New York
articles.summary:
Trump says further talks possible as barrel of Brent crude falls to below $100 for first time in two weeks

Iran has pushed back on claims that it dropped former preconditions for reopening…

blocks.text: Iran has pushed back on claims that it dropped former preconditions for reopening the strait of Hormuz in surprise talks held in New York under the mediation of Qatar between Tehran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

Trump said the three-hour talks held in a room at the UN headquarters had gone very well and been very productive. He suggested further talks were possible imminently, which led to the price of a barrel of Brent crude to fall to below $100 (£75) for the first time in two weeks. Witkoff said the talks had been “encouraging, constructive and successful”.

In his speech to the UN general assembly, Trump said he had a decision to make very soon on whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” or help turn it into one of the great countries of the Middle East, the kind of bombastic threat Trump often deploys during talks with Iran.

In Tehran, the foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei, confirmed the talks had occurred, but appeared not to confirm any shift in the Iranian negotiating position. He said: “The interaction that took place with the American side was through Qatari mediation. This interaction was aimed at conveying Iran’s conditions, including the end of the war in all its dimensions, the cessation of American aggressive actions, the naval siege, and the economic war, the release of Iranian assets and so on.” Aware of the potential domestic backlash, he added that Iran’s conditions had been conveyed.

Iran set seven preconditions before returning to talks, and in a new development over the past 48 hours said the crucial strait of Hormuz could be reopened within seven days if those conditions were met.

It is likely that the US and the Gulf states would have to accept a navigational route for shipping in the strait of Hormuz – a key waterway for transporting oil – that requires commercial shipping to enter through a sea lane mainly in Iranian waters and under Iranian rather than Omani control.

The fact that the talks lasted three hours suggests some progress was made. The US side is under pressure to leverage down oil prices and increase the availability of refined oil before the midterm elections in November. Latest published figures suggest the number of identifiable tankers making it through the strait is fewer than five a day, but estimates of the US navy are much higher.

The blockage in the strait is made worse by the uncertainty surrounding the control by the Houthis’ (the Iranian-backed Yemeni paramilitaries) of a second energy transport chokepoint, the Bab al-Mandab strait that leads from the Red Sea into the Indian Ocean.

There is little sign that Trump wants to relaunch a full-scale war with Iran or indeed with the Houthis as Republicans battle to turn the domestic political agenda away from a hugely unpopular war that the Americans think they are losing.

Iran is under ever more intense pressure from sanctions, and a US naval blockade is making it nearly impossible for Iran to export oil, depriving the country of badly needed foreign currency. Iran’s civilian aircraft on Wednesday faced a potential worldwide grounding owing to the threat of US secondary sanctions on any entity that engaged with Iran’s civilian fleet.

Iranian officials negotiated frantically with neighbouring countries to try to maintain an air bridge, but it appears Oman and Iraq have been forced to close their airspace to Iranian civilian planes.
The president of Iran, Masoud Pezeshkian, is due to address the UN general assembly on Wednesday after arriving in New York on a flight from Tehran as talks were under way.

Pezeshkian is an advocate of negotiations with the US but has not played a direct role in the talks. He has said the memorandum of understanding (MoU), agreed with the US on 17 June, remained the starting point.

Implementation of the MoU fell apart after the two sides accused one another of breaching its terms by trying to take control of the strait. Iran said the MoU clearly left Iran in control of the strait for an interim period before a long-term agreement on its management was reached, including the possibility of Oman and Iran charging fees for navigational services.

Pezeshkian is expected to condemn western double standards over what he regards as an illegal US assault on Iran that has left schoolchildren dead and infrastructure ravaged. Europe’s preparedness to call out Russia for its invasion of Ukraine, and its reticence in criticising the attack on Iran, or Israel’s treatment of Palestinians in Gaza, has been a constant theme of Pezeshkian’s remarks.

Many of the most powerful speeches on Tuesday at the UN general assembly came from European and Arab politicians who decried the inability of the west to enforce peace. In his farewell speech to the UN, the French president, Emmanuel Macron, criticised the attempt to overthrow the Iranian government by the US and Israel, arguing: “Every time a few states, sometimes even in the name of international order, have tried to replace the people in order to change a regime or a system, they have plunged those states into even greater chaos.”

He also said that the west had not imposed a peace in Gaza. “Some boast of a supposed peace. But this peace hasn’t reopened humanitarian routes for a single second. Must we stand by and watch this spectacle that shames us all? Never!”
Macron landed himself in hot water with Israel when he suggested Hamas was not present in the West Bank, as opposed to Gaza.

Netanyahu’s office responded, using the biblical name for the West Bank: “Hamas terrorists carry out attacks against Jews almost every day. They have murdered countless Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria.”

Jordan’s King Abdullah II attacked the Israeli government for “moving the goalposts”, for continuing attacks and the destruction of civilian infrastructure in Gaza, and for refusing to withdraw from the war-torn Palestinian territory. This has forced the Palestinian population in Gaza into barely one-third of the territory, he said.
Observers must no longer treat Israeli policies as “temporary military measures” or a “consequence of war”, he said.
“Accountability begins when we call things what they are: an attempt to erase Palestinian life and impose a new territorial reality in Gaza,” he added.

articles.title: Rome's Colosseum closes after worker falls to his death
articles.summary: The man had been working on a new lighting installation in the iconic Roman amphitheater. Italian authorities said they were working on determining the circumstances of the accident.

image.caption: Rome's Colosseum is the largest amphitheater in the worldImage: Cecilia Fabiano/LaPresse/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The Colosseum in Rome was closed on Wednesday after a worker fell to his death overnight.
Andrea Moretti, 22, died after falling while working on a new lighting installation.
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said she hoped that the cause of the accident would be clarified as soon as possible.

"We are deeply shocked and saddened by the news of the tragic death of Andrea Moretti, a skilled worker who lost his life last night following an accident at the Colosseum," she said. "For a person to die at the age of 22 is unacceptable and even more so when it happens in the workplace."
Italian Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli described the incident as a "tragic event that has left us shocked and stunned."
The Culture Ministry said "the second-tier section where the accident occurred" would be closed
Authorities were working on determining the circumstances of the accident, according to the statement.
The ministry said the site would be fully closed to the public for the day after all visitors leave.
The part of the site where the accident occurred had already been closed early on Wednesday.
What is Rome's Colosseum?
The ancient Colosseum is the world's largest amphitheater.
It was built in the first century under the Roman Empire. It was used to host gladiator fights, executions and animal hunts.
It is one of Rome's most iconic sites and gets up to 20,000 visitors a day at peak times.

articles.title: Hungary: EU Commission wants to unblock €4.2b in funding
articles.summary: The Commission's president has argued that Budapest is strengthening the rule of law with Viktor Orban finally out of office. Funds had been blocked over corruption allegations under Hungary's former…

image.caption: European Commission President von der Leyen says Hungary should be rewarded for reforms undertaken to address standing problemsImage: Omar Havana/REUTERS

blocks.text: The European Commission on Wednesday proposed unlocking some €4.2 billion ($4.8 billion) in frozen funds to be paid out to Hungary.
The cash had been blocked over allegations of corruption tied to Hungary's former government, led by Viktor Orban and his Fidesz party.
"Hungary has taken important steps to strengthen the rule of law and protect the [European] Union's financial interests," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in a statement.

A Commission press release said reforms implemented after Hungary elected Peter Magyar prime minister had addressed "shortcomings in areas such as public procurement, the anti-corruption framework, risks of conflicts of interest and the effectiveness of prosecutorial action."

Orban, a feverent critic of the EU, was often at odds with the bloc over accusations that he and his cronies had undermined rule of law and democracy in the country and that he had engaged in self-dealing and corruption — all charges that he vehemently denied.

The Commission said that steps taken by the new Magyar government to rectify prior problems should result in funds being partially unfrozen and the country once again being allowed to participate in European academic exchange and research programs.
In May, the Commission said it was prepared to unfreeze a total of €16.4 billion in earmarked funds should Budapest make good on its promises to implement all proposed reforms.
EU member states must now approve the Commission's plan.

articles.title: Mass shooting at house party in South Africa leaves 11 dead, 3 wounded: police
articles.summary: Three shooters killed at least 11 people, including a woman who was believed to be pregnant, in an attack at a house party in South Africa, police said Wednesday.

image.caption: A forensic vehicle is parked Wednesday near the scene where 11 people were killed and at least three others injured, in the township of KwaMakhutha, near Durban, South Africa. (Reuterse)

blocks.text: World·New
Three shooters killed at least 11 people, including a woman who was believed to be pregnant, in an attack at a house party in South Africa, police said Wednesday.
People had gathered in home when suspects entered and opened fire, police say
Three others were wounded in the mass shooting late Tuesday night in KwaMakhutha township, about 30 kilometres south of the city of Durban on the country's east coast.

The people had gathered at the house for a party when the suspects entered and opened fire, police said. Ten people, including the pregnant woman, died at the scene and an 11th was declared dead at the hospital.
Authorities did not immediately give out details on the condition of the three people wounded.

items: South Africa's anti-migrant protesters march nationwide after thousands flee violence

blocks.text: Police said they were searching for the attackers and no arrests had been made.

The motive for the shooting was not known, police said, but added that some of the people at the house were known to police as part of investigations into criminal activity. Police said they couldn't give out any more information on those investigations.
"Although the motive of the shooting cannot be confirmed yet, [a] feud between rival groupings cannot be ruled out," police said.

The bodies of some of the victims were laid out on the ground and covered with white sheets outside the small house where the shooting took place. Police cordoned off the larger neighbourhood with yellow tape while forensic investigators worked through the scene.
Police were also investigating if the torching of a car near the house was connected to the shooting.
Killings 'really disturbing,' says premier

Thami Ntuli, the premier of KwaZulu-Natal province, told reporters at the scene that the killings were "really disturbing." He said that there were known problems with drug dealing and illegal firearms in the community.

It's the latest in a series of mass shootings in South Africa in recent years, including one in June when multiple shooters killed 12 people in a poor neighbourhood in Johannesburg. Two mass shootings two weeks apart in December killed 21 people.

South Africa has extremely high rates of violent crime, with official police statistics recording 5,427 homicides in the latest three-month period between April and June, at an average of nearly 60 homicides a day.
Shootings are the most common form of homicide in South Africa, and police and crime experts have long said that one of the biggest problems is a high number of illegal firearms in circulation.

articles.title: [DECODED] When regulation lags, how do organizations protect their truth?
articles.summary: The more advertisers invest in truth, the more trust they build — not just for their respective organizations, but even for our information ecosystem

blocks.text: The more advertisers invest in truth, the more trust they build — not just for their respective organizations, but even for our information ecosystem

items: The Ad Standards Council (ASC) has released guidelines requiring advertisers to maintain human oversight and disclose the use of AI in ads.
Disclosures must be clear and include terms like 'AI-generated' or 'Contains AI-generated content' to promote transparency and help consumers identify AI content.
The ASC's move is seen as a step towards preserving authenticity in advertising and protecting organizations from reputational risks in an era of rapidly developing AI technology.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
In case you missed it, the Ad Standards Council (ASC) released last week its guidelines on the use of artificial intelligence in advertising. ASC’s Circular No. 2026-014 mandates that:

items: Advertisers utilize appropriate human oversight, maintaining full responsibility for all claims and depictions in their respective ads.
Ads created, generated, or materially enhanced using AI include a disclosure.
Disclosures must be clear and reasonably conspicuous, including use of words like “AI-generated,” “AI-assisted,” “Created with AI,” or “Contains AI-generated content.”

blocks.text: Hello, I am Iris B. Gonzales. I started my career in advertising back in 2018. Today, I am a Senior Brand Strategist at The Nerve and am also enrolled at the FEU Institute of Law. I chose both paths because of a growing unease about influence operations and how they affect our information landscape and, ultimately, the democratic systems we seek to uphold.

We at The Nerve have studied how influence operations in the Philippines can mislead audiences, manipulate narratives, and damage organizations’ reputations at scale. These operations now involve synthetic, AI-generated content — and the preliminary report of the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, co-chaired by The Nerve’s Head of Global Strategy Maria Ressa, points out that such content slowly erodes our ability to distinguish authentic from generated content.
That’s a slippery slope toward distrust of media that could otherwise be truthful, termed the “liar’s dividend” in the UN report.

This is why I welcome the ASC’s move to require advertisers to disclose AI use in their content. To be clear, ASC stated that the use of AI by itself doesn’t render an ad misleading or deceptive. The circular merely aims to promote transparency in AI use and compliance with existing laws.

An added benefit, in my view, is that these labels will allow us as consumers to better recognize the tell-tale signs of AI-generated content, and hopefully apply the same discipline to the other content that we consume.

But that discipline only works if the labels are honest in the first place. Advertisers play a crucial role in preserving this authenticity. The more advertisers invest in truth, the more trust they build — not just for their respective organizations, but even for our information ecosystem.

This ASC circular is just one of many discussions we should be having now that AI is developing faster than our ability to measure or govern it. When regulation lags, brands and organizations are often left to police themselves, leaving them vulnerable to reputational risks. For those navigating this shift, the question now becomes: are you ready when that risk hits your organization?

If you’re looking to protect your organization’s reputation in the age of AI, join us in our Crisis Management Masterclass on Friday, October 9. You may also join more of these discussions exploring human values during this year’s Social Good Summit. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Manitoba compensates 2 men switched at birth in 1955 with $250K each in settlement
articles.summary: Two men switched at birth in a rural Manitoba hospital in 1955 were awarded $250,000 each in the 2025-26 fiscal year, according to financial disclosure documents released by the province this week.

image.caption: Edward Ambrose holds up two picture frames. The pictures in his right hand are of his biological parents, whom he never got to meet. The picture in his left hand is a wedding photo of the parents who raised him. (Gary Solilak/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba·New
Two men switched at birth in a rural Manitoba hospital in 1955 were awarded $250,000 each in the 2025-26 fiscal year, according to financial disclosure documents released by the province this week.
Edward Ambrose, Richard Beauvais experienced 'a miscarriage of justice,' provincial cabinet minister says
Two men switched at birth in a rural hospital more than 70 years ago have been compensated $500,000 by the Manitoba government.
Edward Ambrose and Richard Beauvais were awarded $250,000 each in the 2025-26 fiscal year, according to financial disclosure documents released by the province this week.

"Mr. Ambrose and Mr. Beauvais are grateful to the provincial government for the public apology they received from Premier Kinew and for the resolution of their claims for financial compensation," Bill Gange, a lawyer representing both men, told CBC News in a statement.
Ambrose declined to comment when reached by phone Tuesday.
What happened to the two men was "a miscarriage of justice," provincial Justice Minister Matt Wiebe said in a written statement.
"No one can give them back the years that were lost but we hope the settlement brings some closure," he said in the statement.
The men were sent home with the wrong families in 1955 after being born at a hospital in Arborg, about 115 kilometres north of Winnipeg.
Ambrose is Métis but was raised by a Ukrainian family, and Richard Beauvais grew up believing he was of Cree and French descent when his ancestry was actually Ukrainian, Jewish and Polish.
They didn't learn the truth until Ambrose's sister took a 23 and Me DNA test that showed they weren't biologically related. The results did, however, suggest Beauvais was her sibling.

Beauvais was raised near Lake Manitoba in a Métis community. He is a residential school survivor who was removed from his home in the Sixties Scoop, a process that saw an estimated 20,000 First Nation, Inuit and Métis people taken from their families and placed with mostly white families.
Ambrose was raised on a farm in Rembrandt, about 25 kilometres north of Gimli.

"The grief of what we went through, that will always be there — you'll never walk away from that. But for now, I know who I am, and I know who my biological brothers and sisters are. So, it's a step forward to a positive," he told CBC News in 2024.
The two men wanted an apology and compensation. Gange requested both in April 2022.

The apology came in March 2024, about six months after the NDP government was elected in Manitoba and only a couple months after the health minister acknowledged the "devastating" impacts the men experienced.
As Ambrose endeavoured to connect with his biological family and cultural roots, Manitoba Métis Federation president David Chartrand personally handed Ambrose his MMF citizenship card 2½ years ago.
"He's welcomed back to his nation, and he shed tears in that perspective. And he's so pleased to be home," Chartrand told CBC by phone in Ottawa on Tuesday.

"Just imagine what Eddy and them are going through now to try to find their own cultures again and reflect their thoughts and saying, you know, 'This is what I thought I was, this is what I was supposed to have been. And yet I'm somebody else.'"
The MMF president said it was clear from his talks with Ambrose that money was not his primary concern, though Chartrand also feels it's fitting the men were financially compensated.
However, Chartrand questioned whether $250,000 was a fitting amount for what they went through.

items: For man switched at birth, path toward reclaiming lost Métis identity takes a step forward
Manitoba Premier Greg Selinger apologizes for Sixties Scoop

blocks.text: "That's not a lot of money to be somebody else for [decades], and to have never seen your family, your mom and the rest of your family," he said.
"It's definitely a matter [that] clearly still will live with them forever. And the little time they have now, they want to spend as much as they can with the family they have left."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Bryce Hoye is a multi-platform journalist with a background in wildlife biology. He has worked for CBC Manitoba for over a decade with stints producing at CBC's Quirks & Quarks and Front Burner. He was a 2024-25 Knight Science Journalism Fellow at MIT. He is also Prairie rep for outCBC. He has won a national Radio Television Digital News Association award for a 2017 feature on the history of the fur trade, and a 2023 Prairie region award for an audio documentary about a Chinese-Canadian father passing down his love for hockey to the next generation of Asian Canadians.
